story: 78rpm was on the Pickathon bill in 2000.

intro: A Portland songwriter leading his own trio.
story: Casey Neill had put out a self-titled album in 1998 when his trio played Pickathon in 2000. He later made Memory Against Forgetting in 2005 and Brooklyn Bridge in 2007, which No Depression called career-defining and which belongs to New York as much as Portland. Casey Neill & the Norway Rats returned with Subterrene in 2022, their first album in five years, then Sending Up Flares in fall 2023. His solo record time zero land came out on Fluff & Gravy in July 2024, named for a Polaroid camera.

intro: A Portland country-rock band fronted by Elisabeth Ames.
story: Elisabeth Ames formed the Countrypolitans with Coleman of the Freddy Trujillo band as a home for their shared love of roots music, and the band played Pickathon in 2000. Ames cites Merle Haggard and Patsy Cline, and guitarist Hershel Yatovitz of Chris Isaak's band has sat in with them. Ames moved from Portland to Palm Springs for the sun, and the band now plays as Elisabeth Ames and the Countrypolitans.

intro: A Portland country and rock band.
story: The Freak Mountain Ramblers played Pickathon in 2000. Bassist David Reisch later recalled that the name came from a remark about the hills near Plainview, west of Portland, and that Billy Kennedy gave them the use of it. The band ended in January 2016, and a live video of them playing Buckets of Rain in 1999 is posted on Vortex.

intro: A Portland bluegrass and string band.
story: Harebrained, a bluegrass and string band, was on the Pickathon bill in 2000, the second of four straight years.

intro: A slide guitarist from the Pacific Northwest.
story: Kelly Joe Phelps had made Roll Away the Stone in 1997, recorded on a four-track at his Vancouver, Washington, home, and it reached number 10 on Billboard's blues albums chart. Shine Eyed Mister Zen followed in 1999, recorded at home in single takes. Rykodisc released Sky Like a Broken Clock in 2001, Slingshot Professionals in 2003 and Tap the Red Cane Whirlwind in 2005, and he played on Greg Brown's Slant 6 Mind and Further In.

intro: A Portland country singer and her longtime duo partner.
story: Little Sue, the stage name of Susannah Weaver, had a Thursday happy hour at the LaurelThirst from the end of 1995, and she and Lynn Conover played the White Eagle together for about seven years. Her third album, The Long Goodbye, had to be self-released after her label Cravedog folded. No Depression said Weaver had grown up. Conover has played duos with Lowell John and in the Welfare Ranch Rodeo.

intro: A flute and banjo player from the Irish band Solas.
story: Seamus Egan, whose name the lineup spells Eagan, had scored The Brothers McMullen in 1995 and made the solo album When Juniper Sleeps in 1996, the year Solas released its self-titled debut. He has produced records for Antje Duvekot, Liz Carroll and Karan Casey, and released Early Bright in 2020 and Early Bright Live in July 2022.

intro: A Portland Cajun and zydeco dance band.
story: The Too Loose Cajun Zydeco Band, which Portland'5 describes as ever-popular, plays dance music from southwestern Louisiana at festivals, street fairs and weddings across the Pacific Northwest. It was on the Pickathon bill in 2000 and was still playing Portland-area venues in 2024.

intro: A bassist from Leftover Salmon's slamgrass years.
story: Tye North played bass in Leftover Salmon from 1993 to 2000, the band that billed its sound as polyethnic Cajun slamgrass. After leaving he toured with the Portland funk band Porterhouse in fall 2001, recorded with Keller Williams on Laugh, and subbed for the bass player in Michael Hurley's band. He also played with Danny Barnes and assembled his own trio.

intro: A band billed as the Wildcat Wrasslers.
story: The Wildcat Wrasslers were on the Pickathon bill in 2000.

intro: A Portland swing and jazz combo.
story: The Kung Pao Chickens played Pickathon in 2000. McMenamins bills them as Portland's longest-performing gypsy jazz band, active in the Northwest for more than two decades, and Willamette Week named them among the Laurelthirst regulars in 2017. They played a Repeal Day speakeasy party in December 2024 and Edgefield's Little Red Shed in July 2025.
A band billed as toe was on the Pickathon bill in 2000.
